Panther samples random paths and scores each node by how often it shares a path with the source a (outlined). The k = 3 most similar nodes are in the accent color with their scores as badges: c 0.577 and b 0.462 in a's own triangle, then x 0.346 across the bridge. The card ranks them." width="100%"} Panther (Zhang et al., 2015) calls two nodes similar when they often appear on the same paths. It samples many short random paths, each starting at a random node and stepping to a random neighbor (with probability proportional to the edge weight), and scores each node by the share of paths it shares with `source`. Nodes close to the source in a dense part of the graph score highly, so Panther finds the top-$k$ similar nodes on large networks quickly, without the all-pairs work of `simrank_similarity()`. The scores are estimates; pass `seed=` for repeatable results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to compare against, as an ID or label. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How many of the most similar nodes to return. [path_length]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number of steps in each random path ($T$), at least 2. [c]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A positive constant that scales the number of sampled paths. [delta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The probability, between 0 and 1, that the scores miss the `epsilon=` error bound. [epsilon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The error bound on the scores. If `None` (default), $\sqrt{1 / |E|}$, the value the authors recommend. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights for the random steps. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag; edges without a weight count as `1.0`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Up to `k` node IDs (never `source`) with their scores, from most to least similar (ties in node ID order). A score is the share of the sampled paths that pass through both nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source` doesn't exist or is isolated, a parameter is out of range, a weight is negative, or (in a directed graph) a path reaches a node with no out-edges. ::: ## Warns {.doc-warns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [UserWarning]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k` is more than the number of other non-isolated nodes, all of which are returned. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Isolated nodes are dropped first. The number of sampled paths is $R = \lceil (c / \varepsilon^2)(\log_2 \binom{T + 1}{2} + 1 + \ln(1/\delta)) \rceil$, which by the authors' sampling bound makes each score an $\varepsilon$-approximation of its expected value with probability at least $1 - \delta$. Each path of $T$ steps has $T + 1$ nodes (hence $\binom{T + 1}{2}$ pairs of positions) and starts at a uniformly random node, and a score is the number of paths holding both nodes divided by $R$. The sample size follows the fix in NetworkX pull request #8578; NetworkX releases without it use $\lfloor \cdot \rfloor$ and $\binom{T}{2}$, so they sample slightly fewer paths. This follows NetworkX's `panther_similarity`, except that NetworkX picks the top `k` nodes before dropping the source and so returns `k - 1` nodes, while this method returns `k` other nodes. The random paths come from a different generator, so the scores agree with NetworkX's only statistically. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a bridge: the nodes in the source's own triangle score highest. ::: {#b0e401ec .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["a", "b", "c", "x", "y", "z"]) graph.add_edges( [("a", "b"), ("b", "c"), ("c", "a"), ("c", "x"), ("x", "y"), ("y", "z"), ("z", "x")] ) scores = graph.panther_similarity("a", k=3, seed=1) {graph.get_label_from_id(n): round(s, 3) for n, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'c': 0.577, 'b': 0.462, 'x': 0.346} ``` ::: :::
